principle: Choose the least expensive mode whose controls cover the task's evidenced risk and complexity. Escalate on observed triggers, never on prestige.

consequence.description: Blast radius if the in-scope work is wrong: what breaks, who is exposed, is it reversible. This axis alone decides the human gate and independent verification. Mentioning, explaining or planning a critical action is not execution intent and cannot select Full by itself.

critical: external action (deploy, publish, send, push to remote)

breadth.description: How wide the change is: files touched, requirement count, cross-module reach. Breadth buys checkpoints, impact mapping and telemetry - it NEVER buys a human gate by itself. Breadth-only escalation is capped at mode-3-assured.

continuity.description: Whether the work must survive a session boundary. Continuity requires durable checkpoints and session handoff (mode-3 controls); it does not imply high consequence and does not force full.

clarity.description: Whether the task text pins its own acceptance criteria. underspecified = the task implies a real scope (new product/source/adapter/integration/pipeline, 'like the existing X', 'consistent with how the existing sources work') without behavioral sentences pinning edge cases: the real requirements live in the codebase's implicit conventions and must be DISCOVERED before implementation. An underspecified mutating task floors at mode-2-routed and adds the spec-synthesis capability to the selected mode: explore the workspace first, produce a validated spec (surface inventory, convention inventory with file evidence, pinned decision points, risk register with verifications, acceptance tests, frozen requirement ledger), and only then implement. The frozen ledger is the anti-scope-shrink boundary: completion means the full frozen scope passes its acceptance tests; silent narrowing fails the pre-submit gate. Clarity never changes the human gate (consequence only), never selects full, and never fires on read-only, mechanical or documentation-only work.

underspecified: implied-scope phrase (new product/source/adapter/integration, like the existing X) with no pinned behavioral sentences
compiler requirement_count low while breadth/impact phrases (across, end to end, production) are present
material ambiguity terms with thin task text
well-specified: explicit bullets or normative sentences pinning edge cases (exactly, must not, never, raises X)

modes.purpose: Advisory and read-only work: explain, report, assess. Not a runtime target for any mutating task.
modes.notes: Read-heavy review/research answers must still cite the sources they used. The coding benchmark control is separate: an unscaffolded task-only vanilla-control, never this read-only runtime preset.

modes.purpose: Small, reversible, local work with cheap final verification.
Ordinary implementation with precise task modules and objective coverage.
Medium/high-consequence contracts, wide (breadth) work, and anything that must survive a session boundary. The ceiling for breadth-only and continuity-only escalation.
modes.notes: Breadth beyond max_changed_files with low/medium consequence stays here (checkpoints and impact-map absorb width); it does not promote to full. Multi-session work lands here unless a consequence signal independently requires full.

modes.purpose: Critical-consequence work only: outward-facing actions, credential rotation, coordinated production data rollouts, cross-system releases. The human gate and independent verifier exist for blast radius, not for size.

selection_policy: mode = max(consequence floor, breadth floor, continuity floor, clarity floor). Consequence floors: critical->full, high->mode-3, medium->mode-3. Breadth floor: wide->mode-3 (capped there). Continuity floor: multi-session->mode-3 (capped there). Clarity floor: underspecified->mode-2 (capped there); at mode-2 or above an underspecified task additionally receives the spec-synthesis capability on top of the selected mode's capability set (it is a clarity-conditional capability, not a per-mode one, which is why it does not appear in the modes' capability arrays). Only the consequence axis can select full or the human gate.
threshold_status: hypothesis-pending-benchmark: the numeric ceilings (requirement counts, changed-file counts) are uncalibrated priors. The per-mode eval arms in eval-plan.json exist to calibrate them; treat boundary disagreements between the compiler's requirement_count and observed scope as calibration data, not agent failure.

escalation_triggers.condition: an executable in-scope signal from a higher consequence level becomes applicable (credentials, destructive data change, production action, publication, external message)
escalation_triggers.action: raise to that consequence floor immediately (full for critical) and require the relevant human approval; discussion, planning and dry-run intent alone do not trigger Full

escalation_triggers.condition: observed changed-file or requirement count exceeds the selected mode ceiling
escalation_triggers.action: raise one mode before further mutation, but never past mode-3-assured on breadth alone; re-check consequence signals at the same time

escalation_triggers.condition: a material contract ambiguity has no authoritative resolution
escalation_triggers.action: block completion; obtain a decision or test both explicitly permitted interpretations

escalation_triggers.condition: two consecutive verification failures or no-progress cycles
escalation_triggers.action: checkpoint, diagnose and raise one mode or stop

escalation_triggers.condition: work must continue in another session
escalation_triggers.action: raise to mode-3-assured if below it (durable checkpoints and session handoff); do not select full for continuity alone

downgrade_policy: A mode may be lowered only before mutation when evidence disproves the triggering risk. Never downgrade merely to make a gate green.
model_policy: Modes select provider-independent capability profiles. A weekly expiring provider catalog resolves current model selectors; model IDs are never embedded in this policy.
